key.name: suppress-rules
key.summary: Windows that must not be decorated
key.description: Window kinds this extension must leave alone. Keyed by a window-kind fingerprint: '<identity>:client_type=<wayland|x11>,window_type=<int>,has_parent=<bool>,allows_resize=<bool>,attached_dialog=<bool>' e.g. 'wechat:client_type=wayland,window_type=0,has_parent=true,allows_resize=false,attached_dialog=false' The fingerprint is derived from the picked window's stable structural attributes, so a rule never generalizes to every window of an application. Value: which decorations to suppress — 'shadow', 'corners', or 'shadow,corners' for both. Structural disqualifiers (non-decorable window type, maximized/fullscreen) are never affected. Server-side decorated windows keep their native shadow by default but take rounded corners, and either axis may still be moved by a rule. A key present here must not also appear in 'force-rules'; on conflict the suppression wins.

key.name: force-rules
key.summary: Windows that must be decorated anyway
key.description: Window kinds this extension must decorate even when the automatic detection infers that Mutter or the client already draws the decoration. Same key and value format as 'suppress-rules'. This is the escape hatch for what detection cannot see: it may override an inference, never a structural disqualifier. Forcing an axis on a window that really does draw its own decoration doubles it.

key.name: prefer-crisp-text
key.description: Skip rounded corners on fractional scale monitors (retaining shadow) to avoid text blur and resampling overhead.
